model: Leasing-company FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, net debt zero (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: If-converted CB: PV of after-tax coupon saved on conversion (HK$2,155m x 2.68% EIR x (1-15%) = HK$49m/yr, capitalised at CoE - g = 8%)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim note 16; shares_outstanding already includes the 978.2m conversion shares

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run book growth at constant gearing. Set well below the 9.2% 3-yr equity CAGR because the financing book is running off (loan and lease receivables -10.5% in FY2025, financing revenue -14%), management has pivoted from 'scale' to 'quality of incremental deployment', and Pillar Two has reset the tax base; the 2027-28 newbuild wave is the upside to this in the bull case.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 9.2% vs EPS 3-yr CAGR 2.6% and FCF (attributable profit) 3-yr CAGR 3.1%: book is compounding ~3x faster than earnings, i.e. ROE has fallen from 15.6% (FY2022) to 12.6% (FY2025) as funding costs rose and Pillar Two tax arrived. Revenue 5-yr CAGR (16.8%) is flattered by the FY2020 trough base.
historical_growth.notes: fcf CAGRs are computed on attributable net income (the FCFE base before retention), not on reported OCF - capex, which is dominated by loan/lease-book movements and swings sign year to year.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation. The H1 FY2026 windfalls (HK$254m vessel disposal gain, HK$339m JV share from the tanker upcycle) are banked but not repeated; funding cost stays at ~2.8%; the financing book keeps running off while the 23 vessels under construction deliver into long charters, so revenue dips 4% in FY2026 then grows 2-3%; Pillar Two keeps leakage at 15%; the book compounds 3% at constant 1.5-1.6x gearing with the balance paid out (payout ~70% of earnings vs 54% in FY2025). Attributable profit ~HK$2.2bn in FY2026 settling at ~HK$1.9-2.0bn, ROE ~12%, about equal to the 10.5% cost of equity plus a little, which is why the base value sits near 1x if-converted book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rate upcycle persists and the yard pipeline converts. Tanker/LNG strength through 2027 keeps JV income above HK$500m, the shipowner funding gap of the 2027-28 delivery wave is captured through CSSC Group's 63% share of global new orders, funding cost falls to ~2.5% on RMB/HKD channels, impairments stay near zero. Margin 78%, book growth 4-5%, ROE 13-14%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Geopolitical premium unwinds into an oversupplied 2027-28 market. JV income collapses to FY2021 levels, charter rates and residual values fall as record deliveries land, impairments revert to the FY2024 level, the book shrinks for three years and ROE drops to 7-8%. Leverage (1.57x gearing, 63% liabilities/assets) magnifies the earnings hit but the A- ratings and parent funding framework prevent a solvency event; the exit multiple de-rates to 10x FCFE.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A leveraged ship lessor is valued on the cash it can distribute to equity at constant gearing, discounted at a HKD cost of equity, not on unlevered FCF (its OCF is dominated by lease-book movements and its debt is operating funding). The flows are built from profit before tax plus depreciation so every line ties to the income statement, with tax and NCI folded into one leakage rate and retention sized to the scenario's book growth. The if-converted share count is used because the HK$2.39 CB conversion price sits at the current price and below the base value. ROE (12.6% FY2025, 15.9% annualised H1 FY2026 on windfalls) only modestly exceeds the 10.5% cost of equity, so intrinsic value clusters around 1x if-converted book (HK$2.48/share); the scenarios are mostly a view on where mid-cycle ROE settles and on the exit multiple a cyclical lessor is granted.
key_risks_to_valuation: Shipping cycle: JV tanker income (HK$339m in H1 FY2026 vs HK$131m a year earlier) and vessel disposal gains are geopolitically driven and can reverse within a half-year
2027-28 record newbuild deliveries (61m CGT) pressuring charter rates, residual values and re-leasing of the growing operating-lease fleet
Leverage: 1.57x gearing and HK$25bn of borrowings/CB; a 50bp rise in average funding cost costs ~HK$125m pre-tax (~6% of earnings)
Impairments: FY2024 charged HK$447m, FY2025 HK$79m; a downturn returns to the former
Pillar Two global minimum tax (HK$186m in FY2025) and any further tax-base changes on the Hong Kong/PRC leasing structure
Convertible bond: 978m shares at HK$2.39 (16% of the enlarged count); if-converted basis already assumed, not-converted basis is ~10-12% higher per share
SOE governance and US-China sanctions/export-control exposure through the CSSC Group parent
Exit multiple: all three terminal values depend on a buyer paying 10-14x FCFE (7.5-10x earnings) for a cyclical lessor

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (3877.HK) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1.91-2.61
data_sources.financials: 3877.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, HKD millions, FY2018-FY2025 and H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026); H1 FY2026 interim report for the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, EPS note (basic 6,201.3m / diluted 7,039.8m weighted), share capital note (6,204.6m issued), CB note 16 and selected ratios (ROE 15.91%, gearing 1.57x, funding cost 2.78%); FY2025 annual report consolidated income statement and EPS note
data_sources.qualitative: 3877.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-23): business model, revenue mix, guidance, bull/bear cases, risks; FY2025 AR and H1 FY2026 interim outlook sections

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash flow statement: share-based payment HK$(4.4)m (reversal of lapsed options); SBC is immaterial and kept at 0% of revenue in the flows. Dilution from the two option grants (172m, HK$1.15-1.32 strike) is carried in the share count instead (treasury-method 10.7m from the H1 FY2026 EPS note).
inputs.share_count_basis: If-converted fully diluted: 6,204.6m issued at 30 Jun 2026 + 10.7m treasury-method share options (H1 FY2026 EPS note) + 978.2m shares from full conversion of the HK$2,338m 0.75% CB due 2031 at HK$2.39. Held FLAT: SBC is immaterial, there is no buyback, and the CB is already in the count. The CB conversion price (2.39) sits within 2% of the current price and below the base IV, so the if-converted basis is the right one; see inputs.notes for the not-converted alternative.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' driver is a COST OF EQUITY in HKD, applied to post-interest FCFE: HKD risk-free ~3.5% (HK 10y EFN, HKD pegged to USD), equity risk premium 5.5%, beta ~1.2 for a leveraged (gearing 1.57x) cyclical ship lessor = 10.1%, rounded up to 10.5% for SOE-governance and H-share liquidity, consistent with the 10.5% cost of equity used on 0998.HK and 3618.HK. The same 10.5% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, impairment and funding-cost risk are charged once, in the scenario flows, never again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases as operating cost: lease interest (HK$19m/yr) and right-of-use depreciation already sit inside the pre-tax profit that the flows are built from; the HK$297m lease liability is NOT in net debt (net debt is zero in this equity-flow model). Charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Folded into the leakage rate: cash_tax_rate_path is (income tax + NCI profit share) / profit before tax, so NOPAT = profit attributable to equity shareholders. No NCI deduction in the bridge. Calibration: FY2025 PBT 2,219.2 x (1 - 16.9%) = 1,845 = reported attributable profit.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the engine (net_debt = 0). CSSC (HK) Shipping is a leveraged ship lessor / shipping financier: 'profit from operations' is already after finance costs, operating cash flow swings with loan-and-lease-receivable movements (-HK$5.0bn FY2021 to +HK$6.8bn FY2024) and vessel purchases are debt-funded assets of the lease book, so an unlevered owner-FCF DCF does not apply; borrowings are operating funding like a bank's deposits, so net debt is set to zero and the post-interest equity flow is discounted at the cost of equity. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenue (operating lease, finance lease, loan and shipbroking income); ebitda_margin_path = (profit before tax + depreciation) / revenue, i.e. after finance costs, impairments, vessel opex, other income/disposal gains and share of JV/associates (history 67-72% FY2021-FY2025, 92.6% in H1 FY2026 on a HK$254m vessel-disposal gain and a tanker-upcycle JV contribution of HK$339m); da_pct_path = vessel depreciation / revenue (16.5% FY2025, 19.3% H1 FY2026, rising as the 23 vessels under construction deliver); cash_tax_rate_path = (income tax + NCI) / PBT, with OECD Pillar Two (HK$186m added in FY2025) keeping the tax rate near 12% on non-JV profit; capex_pct_path = da_pct_path + equity retention needed to grow the book at the scenario's long-run growth at constant gearing (g x attributable equity: ~12% of revenue base, ~15% bull, ~8% bear), so engine FCF = attributable net income - retained equity = FCFE, the capacity to distribute at constant leverage; wc_capture_pct = 0. last_fcf 1,420 = FY2025 attributable profit 1,845 less 3% x FY2024 opening equity 14,181. NOT STRIPPED, NOT BRIDGED (matching-asset rule): JV interests (HK$1,722m), FVOCI/FVTPL securities (HK$2,706m) and cash all earn income that stays in the flows, so none of them is added in the bridge. CONVERTIBLE BOND: valued if-converted. The flows still carry the CB interest (2.68% EIR on HK$2,155m), so the equity bridge adds the PV of the after-tax coupon saved on conversion (HK$49m/yr at CoE - g = 8%, HK$610m), and the count includes the 978m conversion shares; on a NOT-converted basis (6,215m shares, CB interest in the flows, no bridge item) the per-share values are roughly 10-12% higher, which is the value CB holders capture by converting above HK$2.39. TERMINAL CAP: 13x FCFE base (Gordon at 10.5%/2.5% is 12.8x, so Gordon binds), 14x bull, 10x bear (deliberately binding: a downcycle exit at ~7.5x earnings, the multiple the sector has de-rated to in past troughs). SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, the band collapses. Price is the HKEX regular close of 22 Oct 2026, after the 14 Oct ex-date for the HK$0.05 interim dividend.

bear.narrative: The geopolitical freight premium unwinds in H2 2026 (management's own flagged risk), JV results fall back to the FY2021 level (~HK$50-100m), no further disposal gains, and the 2027-28 newbuild wave (fleet growth 4.4% vs flat ton-mile demand) pushes charter rates and residual values down: re-leasing at lower rates on the growing operating-lease fleet, impairments return to the FY2024 run-rate (~HK$450m, 11% of revenue), USD rates stay high so funding cost stops falling. Revenue shrinks 6%/3%/2% as runoff outpaces new business and management stays 'quality over scale'. Margin troughs at 62% then recovers only to 65%; ROE ~7-8%; retention 8% of revenue for 2% growth. Exit capped at 10x FCFE (~7.5x earnings), the sector's trough multiple. Not a solvency case: A-/A- ratings, 464% NPA coverage and the CSSC Finance RMB10bn framework hold.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue -4% (H1 -5.3%: financing-book runoff, partly offset by H2 deliveries), then +2-3% as the 23 newbuilds under construction and a modest share of the 2027-28 shipowner funding gap replace run-off. Margin 85% in FY2026 (H1 disposal gain and JV tanker upcycle already booked; H2 JV share ~HK$200m, no further disposal gains) normalising to 74%, above the 67-72% FY2021-25 history because the comprehensive funding cost has fallen from 3.5% to 2.78%. Depreciation rises to 20% of revenue as operating-lease mix grows. Leakage 15% (Pillar Two + NCI). Retention 12% of revenue funds 3% book growth at constant 1.5-1.6x gearing. Implied attributable profit ~HK$2.2bn FY2026, ~HK$1.9-2.0bn mid-cycle (ROE ~12%).

bull.narrative: Tanker/LNG rate strength persists through 2027 (Hormuz/Red Sea re-routing becomes semi-permanent), JV contribution stays HK$500m+/yr and vessels keep being sold into cycle-high values; funding cost falls toward 2.5% on RMB/CB channels and a lower-rate USD curve; the 2027-28 record delivery wave (61m CGT) is captured as new origination through the CSSC Group yard pipeline, so the book grows 4-5% from 2027; impairments stay near zero on ~100% collection. Margin settles at 78%, ROE ~13-14%; retention 15% of revenue funds the faster growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the H1 FY2026 earnings strength is, by management's own account, geopolitically rather than fundamentally driven, the 2027-28 newbuild wave is a dated, visible supply shock, and 1.57x gearing magnifies any earnings miss. Bull cut to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold at once: the rate premium persisting AND funding costs continuing to fall while USD rates stay elevated. Base 50%: the business has a 7-7.5 year average remaining charter book, ~100% collection and a falling funding cost, so mid-cycle normalisation is the most likely path.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
